source.title: Nonlinear Behaviour of Critical Points for a Simple Neural Network

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text appears to contain the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes critical points and approximation quality for a one-dimensional shallow ReLU network, but does not test the listed classification-error, depth, initialization, learning-rate, or normalization versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on zero training loss and spurious minima; those cited results are not rows. Its own theorems and numerical experiment concern function approximation, not training classification error on the named benchmarks.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes continuous L2 approximation by shallow one-dimensional ReLU networks. It does not test any listed version. In particular, its unfavorable-critical-point construction does not measure gradient-descent failure frequencies in realizable teacher-student problems or the effect of adding one or two student neurons required by V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The conditional guarantees concern adaptive approximation within convex or concave subdomains; allocation between subdomains can remain suboptimal. The study leaves proving that gradient descent reaches critical points satisfying the resolution assumptions to future work. Its preliminary cusp experiment shows breakpoint adaptation with slow convergence.
record.recipe_differences: A theoretical analysis of continuous L2 loss for a one-dimensional shallow ReLU network, with one preliminary gradient-descent experiment on a sampled function-approximation task; it is not a classification benchmark recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantees depend on local breakpoint resolution and on the target being convex or concave on the considered subdomains; the experiment reports uniform and random initial biases in Figure 3 but gives no quantitative comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Under local resolution and smoothness assumptions, critical points equidistribute local target smoothness and achieve adaptive L2 approximation bounds on convex or concave subdomains. Unresolved target oscillations permit arbitrarily large critical-point approximation error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Critical-point approximation quality in shallow one-dimensional ReLU networks depends on local breakpoint resolution of target features.

fits_no_version.finding: For the width-16 cusp approximation experiment, gradient descent moves breakpoints toward the cusp, but convergence remains qualitatively slow over 100000 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent can adapt breakpoint locations toward difficult target features while converging slowly in one-dimensional function approximation.

record.problems: The numerical experiment is described as preliminary, reports no numerical training-error values, and provides no uncertainty estimates. The main claims are theoretical and conditional on smoothness, local resolution, and convex or concave subdomains; they do not establish classification-error outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results were left out. Cited findings from prior studies were excluded.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional classification training on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, label corruption, and effects of size, stopping, or regularization.
All parts: realizable ReLU teacher-student problems, gradient-descent failure frequencies as teacher and student widths grow together, and adding one or two student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, training speed, and trainable depth.
All parts: learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
All parts: batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because these rows measure different properties; this does not dispute the reported theorems or qualitative experiment. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, stopping, and regularization recipes are not tested.
No teacher-student setup, width comparison, or gradient-descent frequency of spurious minima is tested.

No comparison of activation-matched or orthogonal initializations, training speed, or trainable depth is tested.
No learning-rate stability threshold, curvature, or loss-divergence experiment is tested.

rows.value: Breakpoints move toward the cusp; convergence is very slow and requires a substantial number of epochs.

Uniform and random initial biases appear in separate Figure 3 panels, but no activation-matched initialization comparison or quantitative training-speed difference is reported. The original partial state has no applicable claim version.
